newsitem.title: POLAND: EBRD, two Polish banks in joint $30 mln programme.
newsitem.headline: EBRD, two Polish banks in joint $30 mln programme.

text.p: Two Polish state-owned commercial banks will provide funds for a European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) financial restructuring programme for medium-sized Polish firms, the EBRD said in a statement on Friday.

Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA of Lublin and Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA of Warsaw will provide $15 million, the same amount as the EBRD itself is contributing to the programme, which is eventually expected to reach $80 million.
Equity investments of $1-4 million will be made in selected medium-sized companies. Hands-on expertise and technical support in restructuring will be provided.

"The programme is driven by the need to find a permanent viable solution for the participating enterprises and will seek to sell the investment once the firms have been successfully stabilised," the statement said.
Other Polish banks are expected to participate in the scheme. The European Union's PHARE aid programme is due to add $12 million.
